name: empty
why: No arguments. Every semantics admits exactly the empty set.

name: single_unattacked
why: An unattacked argument is accepted by every semantics.

name: simple_defeat
why: a attacks b and nothing attacks a, so a is in and b is out.

name: even_cycle_two
why: a and b attack each other. Grounded is empty (neither is forced). Two preferred and two stable extensions, one per argument. This is the shape that produces the 'Worth adding' tier.

name: odd_cycle_three
why: a->b->c->a. Grounded is empty. There is NO stable extension, which is the classic reason stable alone is not enough. The only preferred extension is the empty set.

name: self_attack
why: a attacks itself, so it can never be in a conflict-free set. No stable extension exists because nothing attacks a from outside.

name: self_attacker_attacks_other
why: a attacks itself and also b. a can never be in. b is attacked by a, and a is never defeated by any admissible set, so b is never defended. Grounded and the sole preferred extension are both empty, and there is no stable extension.

name: reinstatement
why: a->b->c. a is unattacked so it is in; that defeats b; with b defeated, c is defended and reinstated. Grounded is {a,c}. This is the mechanism by which evidence moves an argument to Solid ground.

name: floating_defeat
why: a and b attack each other and both attack c. Whichever of a or b survives, c is defeated, so c is in no preferred extension even though grounded is empty. c is genuinely 'Left out'.

name: two_independent_cycles
why: Two separate 2-cycles. Preferred extensions are the four combinations, one choice from each cycle. Checks that the solver does not collapse independent choices.

name: cycle_plus_unattacked
why: An unattacked argument alongside a 2-cycle. Grounded holds the unattacked one only; each preferred extension adds one side of the cycle.

name: longer_reinstatement_chain
why: a->b->c->d. a in, b out, c reinstated, d defeated by c. Grounded is {a,c}. Checks the monotone iteration runs more than one round.

name: insurer_reason_with_one_unanswered_rebuttal
why: The product's own shape. The insurer's reason i is attacked by counter-argument s; s is in a mutual attack with the insurer's known rebuttal r. Grounded is empty, and s appears in one preferred extension, which is exactly the Worth adding tier.

name: insurer_reason_with_answered_rebuttal
why: The same shape once the user attaches the evidence. The answer e attacks the rebuttal r one-way. e is unattacked so it is in; r is defeated; s is reinstated and defeats i. Grounded is {e,s}, which is the Solid ground tier.
